_comment: Citable loan-program rules, one entry per rule, referenced from posts with
a [[RULE:key]] marker. Same architecture as neighborhoods.json: the volatile
thing lives in one data file and the posts carry markers, so refreshing the
whole site after a handbook update is one edit rather than forty.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. A page on a licensed originator's site that asserts
'FHA requires X' and is eighteen months stale is worse than a page that
says nothing, because the reader acts on it and the NMLS number at the
bottom is a real person's. Every rule here therefore carries three things:
the handbook section it comes from, the date a human verified it against
that section, and the text itself. Nothing is written from memory.
THREE RENDER STATES, all handled by gen/guidelines.py:
1. verifiedOn is null -> the page renders an honest line saying the current
requirement is confirmed per file, with a phone number. It does NOT
state a number. This is the default and it is deliberately safe, so a
post can publish before anyone has opened the handbook.
2. verifiedOn is recent -> renders the rule, the handbook citation and the
verification date.
3. verifiedOn older than STALE_DAYS -> renders the rule plus a visible
notice saying how old the verification is.
HOW A RULE GETS VERIFIED. Open the cited handbook section, read it, and
record what it actually says. Then run:
python gen/verify_guideline.py <key> --section '<cite>' --text '<rule>'
That stamps verifiedOn with today and writes the text. Never hand-edit a
verifiedOn date, and never stamp a rule you did not read.
THE OVERLAY DISTINCTION, which is the whole point of the content strategy.
The handbook is a floor, not the market. Investors layer their own stricter
requirements on top, and the gap between the two is where a borrower
actually lives. `handbookFloor` is the published rule. `overlayReality` is
what lenders actually do, which is Ricky's observation and is labelled as
such rather than presented as a published requirement. Keep them separate.
Conflating them is how a page becomes wrong.
SOURCES. FHA rules cite the HUD Single Family Housing Policy Handbook
4000.1, which is a US government work and free to quote. VA cites the
Lenders Handbook M26-7. Conventional cites the Fannie Mae Selling Guide or
the Freddie Mac Seller/Servicer Guide. Cite the section, not just the
document.

ruleSchema.program: FHA | VA | USDA | Conventional | Jumbo | Non-QM
ruleSchema.topic: credit | income | assets | collateral | employment | residency | obligations | process
ruleSchema.question: The rule in borrower language, used as the aside heading.
ruleSchema.handbookFloor: What the published guideline says. Null until verified.
ruleSchema.section: The citation, e.g. 'Handbook 4000.1 II.A.4.b'. Null until verified.
ruleSchema.verifiedOn: YYYY-MM-DD, the date a human read that section. Null by default.
ruleSchema.overlayReality: Optional. What investors actually do, labelled as Ricky's observation, not as a published rule.
ruleSchema.judgmentNeeded: Optional note on what Ricky still has to add to the page.

fha-203k-renovation.question: Can an FHA loan cover repairs?
fha-203k-renovation.handbookFloor: Section 203(k) is FHA's renovation program, financing a purchase and the improvements together and sizing the loan on the completed value. It is the route for a property that cannot pass as-is, and HUD REO properties that do not qualify for Section 203(b) are eligible only under 203(k).
fha-203k-renovation.section: HUD Handbook 4000.1 Section 203(k), verified against a wholesale FHA guideline current to 2026-10-15
fha-203k-renovation.overlayReality: This is the clearest overlay in the whole program. The lender matrix I verified this against states plainly that it does not originate or purchase 203(k) transactions at all. FHA offers the program; that investor will not do it. A borrower told renovation financing is not available was told one shelf's answer, and placing a 203(k) is a matter of finding a lender who does them.
fha-203k-renovation.judgmentNeeded: Who do you actually place 203(k) files with, and how much longer do they take?

fha-appraisal-repairs.question: What will an FHA appraiser make the seller fix?
fha-appraisal-repairs.judgmentNeeded: The listing-agent angle: which FHA appraisal call-outs most often blow up a resale, and how do you get ahead of them?

fha-bankruptcy-waiting-period.question: How long after a bankruptcy can I get an FHA loan?
fha-bankruptcy-waiting-period.handbookFloor: Chapter 7 must be discharged 24 months before the case number assignment date. Chapter 13 must have been entered at least 12 months before the case number assignment date with payments made as agreed. Exceptions for documented extenuating circumstances are considered case by case.
fha-bankruptcy-waiting-period.section: HUD Handbook 4000.1, verified against Part F of a wholesale FHA guideline current to 2026-10-15
fha-bankruptcy-waiting-period.judgmentNeeded: Have you closed one during an active Chapter 13, and what did the trustee letter need to say?
fha-bankruptcy-waiting-period.overlayReality: Two investor additions matter here. The matrix I verified this against requires a Chapter 13 plan to be paid out and discharged before closing and will not allow loan proceeds to pay off a bankruptcy balance, where FHA itself contemplates closing during an active plan with court or trustee approval. It also does not permit FHA's Back to Work extenuating circumstances program at all. So a borrower told no on an active Chapter 13 has been told that lender's answer, not FHA's.

fha-caivrs-federal-debt.question: Can unpaid federal debt stop my FHA loan?
fha-caivrs-federal-debt.handbookFloor: Every borrower must pass a HUD Credit Alert Interactive Voice Response System check, known as CAIVRS, which screens for delinquent federal debt and prior FHA insurance claims. Lenders must also confirm that parties to the transaction do not appear on the SAM Excluded Parties List or HUD's Limited Denial of Participation list. A valid Social Security number is required; other forms of taxpayer identification are not accepted.
fha-caivrs-federal-debt.section: HUD Handbook 4000.1, verified against Part A of a wholesale FHA guideline current to 2026-10-15
fha-caivrs-federal-debt.overlayReality: CAIVRS is not your credit report, and that is why this ambushes people. A defaulted federal student loan can have dropped off a credit report years ago and still return a CAIVRS hit, which makes a borrower with a clean report and a good score ineligible until it is resolved. Rehabilitation or consolidation out of default takes months, so this is the first thing to raise rather than the last.
fha-caivrs-federal-debt.judgmentNeeded: How many files have you seen stopped by a CAIVRS hit the borrower had no idea about?

fha-cash-out-refinance.question: How much equity can I take out with an FHA cash-out refinance?
fha-cash-out-refinance.judgmentNeeded: Worth saying when FHA cash-out beats a conventional cash-out and when it clearly does not.
fha-cash-out-refinance.handbookFloor: FHA cash-out refinancing is capped at 80% loan-to-value. If the property was listed for sale it must have been off the market at least six months before the application, where a rate-and-term refinance only requires it to be off the market one day before application.
fha-cash-out-refinance.section: HUD Handbook 4000.1, verified against Part Q of a wholesale FHA guideline current to 2026-10-15
fha-cash-out-refinance.overlayReality: The six month seasoning after a listing is the one that catches people. A seller who gives up, pulls the listing and decides to take equity out instead cannot do a cash-out for half a year. A rate-and-term is available almost immediately, so if the goal is a lower payment rather than cash, there is a path now.

fha-cash-to-close-sourcing.question: Where can my down payment and closing costs come from?
fha-cash-to-close-sourcing.handbookFloor: Every dollar of cash to close must be sourced and documented. Asset verification must be current, and where a third-party verification service is used the data has to be current within 30 days of the verification date. Cash that cannot be traced to a documented source cannot be used, which is why cash deposits are generally unusable and why any large or unusual deposit is questioned.
fha-cash-to-close-sourcing.section: HUD Handbook 4000.1, verified against Part H of a wholesale FHA guideline current to 2026-10-15
fha-cash-to-close-sourcing.judgmentNeeded: Worth one line on the largest deposit you have had to source and what finally satisfied it.

fha-child-support-income.question: Does child support or alimony count as income?
fha-child-support-income.handbookFloor: Alimony and child support are recognised sources of effective income when properly verified and documented, alongside pensions, Social Security, disability, trust income and others. Effective income must be shown to be reasonably likely to continue for at least the first three years of the loan, which is the test that matters for support with an end date.
fha-child-support-income.section: HUD Handbook 4000.1, verified against Part G of a wholesale FHA guideline current to 2026-10-15
fha-child-support-income.overlayReality: The continuation test is what decides this. Child support with a termination date inside three years contributes little or nothing to qualifying, however reliably it arrives today. Get the order and the payment history from the state disbursement records early, because a documented history is the difference between income and a number nobody will count.
fha-child-support-income.judgmentNeeded: Does Arizona's clearinghouse payment history satisfy underwriting cleanly, or do you need more?

fha-child-support-obligation.question: How does child support I pay affect what I qualify for?
fha-child-support-obligation.handbookFloor: Support you pay is a monthly obligation and is included in your liabilities for the debt-to-income calculation. It appears in credit reporting, in the decree and as a recurring withdrawal in bank statements, so it is found whether or not it is disclosed. Arrears are a separate and more serious matter than the monthly amount.
fha-child-support-obligation.section: HUD Handbook 4000.1, verified against Part I of a wholesale FHA guideline current to 2026-10-15
fha-child-support-obligation.judgmentNeeded: Disclose on call one. Worth saying how often an undisclosed obligation surfaces late and what it costs.

fha-collections-judgments.question: Do I have to pay off collections and judgments?
fha-collections-judgments.handbookFloor: Collection accounts are evaluated against a cumulative balance threshold rather than individually, and in a community property state the collection accounts of a non-borrowing spouse are included in that cumulative balance and analyzed as part of your ability to pay, unless state law excludes them. Judgments of a non-borrowing spouse in a community property state generally must be resolved. Disputed derogatory accounts are treated differently again, and a non-borrowing spouse's disputed accounts are not counted toward the cumulative balance.
fha-collections-judgments.section: HUD Handbook 4000.1, verified against Part F of a wholesale FHA guideline current to 2026-10-15
fha-collections-judgments.overlayReality: Arizona is a community property state, so this matters here in a way it does not in most of the country. A spouse who is not on the loan can still bring collections and judgments into the analysis. If your spouse is staying off the application to protect the file, their derogatory credit may follow it anyway, and that is worth finding out in week one.
fha-collections-judgments.judgmentNeeded: Arizona community property angle is strong. Have you had a non-borrowing spouse's collections change a file?

fha-condo-approval.question: Does the condo have to be FHA approved?
fha-condo-approval.handbookFloor: Other than on a streamline refinance, the condominium project must be HUD approved and the approval must not be expired at the time the case number is issued. HUD publishes a searchable list of approved projects, so the status of a specific building is checkable before you write an offer rather than discovered in underwriting.
fha-condo-approval.section: HUD Handbook 4000.1, verified against Part J of a wholesale FHA guideline current to 2026-10-15
fha-condo-approval.judgmentNeeded: Have you used single-unit approval, and how long did it actually take?
fha-condo-approval.overlayReality: The lender matrix I verified this against states it will not process a DELRAP, the lender-driven review by which a project can be approved directly. So at that investor an unapproved building is simply unapproved; there is no path to get it reviewed. Whether your originator will pursue project or single-unit approval is therefore a question worth asking out loud, because the answer varies and most buyers never ask.

fha-departing-residence.question: I am keeping my current home. Does that payment count against me?
fha-departing-residence.judgmentNeeded: This is one of the widest overlay spreads there is. Which investors let a lease and a documented deposit exclude the old payment, and which make you close the sale first?

fha-disaster-area-reinspection.question: My area had a wildfire or flood. Does the appraisal have to be redone?
fha-disaster-area-reinspection.judgmentNeeded: Arizona-relevant for wildfire and monsoon flooding. Have you had a closing held for a disaster re-inspection, and how long did it add?

fha-dti-limits.question: What debt-to-income ratio will FHA allow?
fha-dti-limits.handbookFloor: On a file that receives an automated approval the maximum debt-to-income ratio is whatever the automated underwriting system returns, rather than a single published ceiling. Manually underwritten files must meet HUD's own manual requirements, where the ratio limits are tighter and documented compensating factors are what allow a file above the baseline.
fha-dti-limits.section: HUD Handbook 4000.1 Chapter 5, verified against the Qualifying Ratios section of a wholesale FHA guideline current to 2026-10-15
fha-dti-limits.judgmentNeeded: How often does an exception review come back approved, and what makes the difference?
fha-dti-limits.overlayReality: The investor layer is where this gets real. The matrix I verified this against requires an internal exception review for any FHA file with a qualifying score below 660 where both ratios exceed 37 and 47. Both have to exceed, so a 39 and 50 goes to review and a 39 and 43 does not. That is an extra approval step most borrowers never hear about, and it is the kind of thing that turns a yes into a maybe.

fha-ead-work-authorization.question: What work authorization documents do I need as a non-citizen?
fha-ead-work-authorization.judgmentNeeded: Documentation is where these stall. What do you ask for on the first call to avoid a week-three surprise?

fha-employment-gap.question: I changed jobs or had a gap. Does that disqualify me?

fha-foreclosure-waiting-period.question: How long after a foreclosure or short sale?
fha-foreclosure-waiting-period.handbookFloor: A foreclosure must be settled a minimum of 36 months before the case number assignment date. The same three year measure applies to a transfer of title through a foreclosure sale, a deed in lieu of foreclosure, and a pre-foreclosure or short sale. The clock runs from the transfer of title, not from the filing.
fha-foreclosure-waiting-period.section: HUD Handbook 4000.1, verified against Part F of a wholesale FHA guideline current to 2026-10-15
fha-foreclosure-waiting-period.overlayReality: Exceptions for extenuating circumstances exist but at this investor require corporate credit approval, which is a real process rather than an underwriter's discretion. Expect to produce independent third-party evidence of the event, not an explanation.
fha-foreclosure-waiting-period.judgmentNeeded: People routinely count from the wrong date. Worth a line on how often the recorded trustee's deed date differs from what the borrower believes.

fha-gift-funds.question: Can the FHA down payment be a gift?
fha-gift-funds.handbookFloor: For funds to count as a gift there must be no expected or implied repayment to the donor. The lender must establish both that the gift did not come from an unacceptable source and that the money was the donor's own funds, which is why the donor's bank statement is requested and why the request is not optional. Timing of when the gift reached you does not remove that requirement.
fha-gift-funds.section: HUD Handbook 4000.1, verified against Part H of a wholesale FHA guideline current to 2026-10-15
fha-gift-funds.judgmentNeeded: Which donor documentation request kills the most deals in practice?
fha-gift-funds.overlayReality: One trap worth knowing: on a manually underwritten file, surplus gift funds may not be counted as cash reserves. So a borrower whose entire cash position is a gift can satisfy the down payment and still fail the reserve test, and manual underwriting is exactly where reserves matter most.

fha-identity-of-interest.question: Can I buy a house from a family member with an FHA loan?
fha-identity-of-interest.judgmentNeeded: Non-arm's length purchases get extra scrutiny. What have you actually had to produce to close one?

fha-loan-limit-maricopa.question: What is the FHA loan limit in Maricopa County?
fha-loan-limit-maricopa.handbookFloor: FHA sets a maximum loan amount by county and revises it annually, and the programs distinguish standard loan amounts from high balance loan amounts, which are the amounts above the standard limit in higher-cost counties. Because the figure changes every year, the current Maricopa County limit should be read from HUD rather than from any page that hardcodes it, including this one.
fha-loan-limit-maricopa.section: HUD published county loan limits, cross-checked against the standard and high balance tiers of a wholesale FHA guideline current to 2026-10-15
fha-loan-limit-maricopa.judgmentNeeded: This needs a yearly refresh, not a one-time verification. Worth a calendar reminder each January.
fha-loan-limit-maricopa.overlayReality: High balance files carry extra conditions at the investor level. The matrix I verified this against requires a maximum of one 30-day late in 12 months on mortgage history and an automated approval for every high balance loan, where a streamline may still be manually underwritten. So crossing into high balance territory tightens the file, not just the price.

fha-manual-underwrite.question: What is a manual underwrite and why am I in one?
fha-manual-underwrite.handbookFloor: A file is downgraded from the automated evaluation to a manual underwrite on defined triggers rather than at random. They include a transfer of title through foreclosure or deed in lieu within three years of the case number assignment date, a mortgage payment history on any reported trade line that requires a downgrade, undisclosed mortgage debt, and business income showing a decline greater than 20 percent over the analysis period. Once manual, the file must meet HUD's requirements for manually underwritten loans and compensating factors begin to matter.
fha-manual-underwrite.section: HUD Handbook 4000.1, verified against Part F of a wholesale FHA guideline current to 2026-10-15
fha-manual-underwrite.judgmentNeeded: Which compensating factors actually move an underwriter on a manual file?
fha-manual-underwrite.overlayReality: The business income trigger is the one that blindsides self-employed borrowers. A year over year decline past 20 percent moves the file to manual underwriting on its own, which tightens the ratio limits at exactly the moment the qualifying income also fell. Two bad things arrive together and neither is obvious in advance.

fha-min-credit-score.question: What credit score does FHA actually require?
fha-min-credit-score.handbookFloor: A minimum decision credit score of 580 reaches FHA's maximum financing, a 96.50% loan-to-value on a purchase. Scores from 500 to 579 are eligible at a reduced loan-to-value, which means a larger down payment. The rate-and-term and simple refinance maximum is 97.75% loan-to-value, and cash-out is capped at 80%.
fha-min-credit-score.section: HUD Handbook 4000.1, confirmed against the Loan Matrix of a wholesale FHA guideline current to 2026-10-15
fha-min-credit-score.judgmentNeeded: Lowest score you have actually closed, and how many investors would touch it.
fha-min-credit-score.overlayReality: The lender matrix I verified this against sets its own floor at 580 for every transaction type and offers no 500 to 579 tier at all, and it also requires an automated underwriting approval. So FHA's published floor of 500 is not available there at any down payment. That is the overlay, and it is why the number you read online is not your real minimum.

fha-mip-duration.question: How long do I pay FHA mortgage insurance?
fha-mip-duration.handbookFloor: The upfront premium is 175 basis points, 1.75%, of the base loan amount, financed or paid in cash. The annual premium runs for a period set by your original loan-to-value: at 90% or below it is assessed for the first 11 years of the term or until the end of the term, whichever comes first; above 90%, which includes every minimum-down-payment file, it is assessed for 30 years or the end of the term. This applies to case numbers assigned on or after June 3, 2013. Above 90% the only reliable exit is refinancing out of FHA.
fha-mip-duration.section: HUD Handbook 4000.1, Part M of a wholesale FHA guideline current to 2026-10-15
fha-mip-duration.judgmentNeeded: The refinance-out-of-FHA play: when does it make sense at today's rates and when does the rate difference swamp the insurance saving?

fha-non-occupant-coborrower.question: Can a parent co-sign an FHA loan?
fha-non-occupant-coborrower.handbookFloor: A non-occupying co-borrower or cosigner is permitted on an FHA purchase. Cash-out refinancing is not permitted where one is used. The co-borrower may not be an interested party to the sales transaction, which rules out the seller, the builder or the agent.
fha-non-occupant-coborrower.section: HUD Handbook 4000.1, verified against the Non-Occupant Co-Borrower section of a wholesale FHA guideline current to 2026-10-15
fha-non-occupant-coborrower.overlayReality: The matrix I verified this against expects overall transaction ratios generally not to exceed 31 and 43 when a non-occupying co-borrower is used, with higher ratios considered where the co-borrower's financial strength is established. That is tighter than the ratios an occupying borrower alone would face, so adding a parent can bring the ceiling down as well as the income up. Worth modelling both ways before anyone signs.
fha-non-occupant-coborrower.judgmentNeeded: Have you seen adding a co-borrower actually hurt a file because of the tighter ratio expectation?

fha-non-permanent-resident.question: Can I get an FHA loan without being a US citizen?
fha-non-permanent-resident.judgmentNeeded: Work authorization documentation is where these stall. What do you ask for on the first call?

fha-number-of-borrowers.question: How many people can be on an FHA loan together?
fha-number-of-borrowers.judgmentNeeded: A good teaching example: caps here have historically been investor overlays rather than the federal rule, and they move. Worth using to show the reader the difference.

fha-occupancy-requirement.question: Do I have to live in the house?
fha-occupancy-requirement.handbookFloor: FHA insures owner-occupied housing, and eligible property types are one to four family dwellings, planned unit developments, townhomes, row homes, modular homes and HUD approved condominiums, with manufactured homes eligible under a separate addendum. Streamline refinances are the exception that may be done on owner occupied, HUD approved secondary residences and non-owner-occupied properties.
fha-occupancy-requirement.section: HUD Handbook 4000.1, verified against Part C of a wholesale FHA guideline current to 2026-10-15
fha-occupancy-requirement.judgmentNeeded: Occupancy misrepresentation is the line people cross without realising. Worth one blunt sentence.

fha-secondary-financing-dpa.question: Can I combine FHA with down payment assistance?
fha-secondary-financing-dpa.judgmentNeeded: DPA programs stack onto FHA constantly in Arizona and each has its own rules. Which ones do you actually see work, and where do they break?

fha-self-employed-history.question: How long do I need to be self-employed for an FHA loan?
fha-self-employed-history.handbookFloor: Qualifying income must be shown to be reasonably likely to continue for at least the first three years of the loan, and every file carries an income worksheet setting out the rationale behind the calculation. For a self-employed borrower that means the figure is derived and documented rather than stated, and you are entitled to see how it was reached.
fha-self-employed-history.section: HUD Handbook 4000.1, verified against Part G of a wholesale FHA guideline current to 2026-10-15
fha-self-employed-history.judgmentNeeded: The same-industry exception for under two years: how have you documented prior experience successfully?
fha-self-employed-history.overlayReality: Ask for the income worksheet. It is a required document, it shows the arithmetic that produced your qualifying income, and almost no borrower knows to ask for it. If the number came out lower than you expected, the worksheet is where you find out whether an add-back was missed or a year was treated as the qualifying figure.

fha-seller-concession-limit.question: How much can the seller pay toward my FHA closing costs?
fha-seller-concession-limit.handbookFloor: Interested parties may contribute up to 6 percent of the sales price toward the borrower's origination fees, other closing costs and discount points. Everything an interested party pays counts against that one limit, including any interest rate buydown, so a seller funding a buydown and the buyer's closing costs is spending from the same 6 percent. Premium pricing used to pay actual closing costs or prepaid items is treated separately and does not count against the limit, but it cannot be used to pay off debts, collections, escrow shortages or judgments.
fha-seller-concession-limit.section: HUD Handbook 4000.1, Part S of a wholesale FHA guideline current to 2026-10-15
fha-seller-concession-limit.judgmentNeeded: How often does the 6 percent cap bind before the seller's willingness does, at a typical Scottsdale price point?
fha-seller-concession-limit.overlayReality: The matrix also caps total sales incentive, including commissions and finder's fees, at 8 percent of the sales price, and it prohibits raising the sales price after the appraisal in order to create a seller credit. Those are the lender's own rules rather than FHA's, and the second one catches deals that try to manufacture concession room late.

fha-streamline-refinance.question: What is an FHA streamline refinance?
fha-streamline-refinance.handbookFloor: A streamline refinance carries reduced documentation and is the one FHA transaction available on a non-owner-occupied property or a HUD approved secondary residence as well as a primary home. Non-owner-occupied properties and HUD approved secondary residences may only be streamline refinanced into a fixed rate mortgage. A streamline stays inside FHA, so the mortgage insurance structure continues; it lowers a rate, it does not escape the premium.
fha-streamline-refinance.section: HUD Handbook 4000.1, verified against Part Q of a wholesale FHA guideline current to 2026-10-15
fha-streamline-refinance.judgmentNeeded: People conflate a streamline with escaping MIP. Worth being blunt that it does not.

fha-student-loan-payment.question: How is a student loan payment counted if it is deferred or on an income-driven plan?
fha-student-loan-payment.handbookFloor: Regardless of payment status, including deferment and forbearance, the monthly obligation counted is either the payment shown on the credit report or the actual documented payment when that is above zero, or 0.5 percent of the outstanding loan balance when the reported payment is zero. The payment can be excluded entirely only with written documentation from the servicer or program that the balance has been forgiven, cancelled, discharged or paid in full. Deferment does not mean excluded.
fha-student-loan-payment.section: HUD Handbook 4000.1, verified against Part F of a wholesale FHA guideline current to 2026-10-15
fha-student-loan-payment.judgmentNeeded: Have you moved a file by getting a servicer to document an actual payment instead of letting the 0.5 percent apply?
fha-student-loan-payment.overlayReality: The practical effect is the half-percent rule. A borrower deferred at zero has 0.5 percent of the balance counted against them, which on a six-figure balance is a payment far above what they pay today. That single line decides how much house a lot of people qualify for, and it is why documenting an actual payment above zero with the servicer can be worth more than anything else in the file.

fha-temporary-buydown.question: Can a seller fund a temporary rate buydown on an FHA loan?
fha-temporary-buydown.judgmentNeeded: This is the bridge between the FHA cluster and the seller and listing-agent cluster. Worth a line on how often you use a 2-1 versus a 3-2-1 on an FHA purchase.
fha-temporary-buydown.handbookFloor: Temporary buydowns are permitted on FHA. Available structures include 3-2-1, 2-1, 1-1 and 1-0. They are limited to a primary residence, a purchase rather than a refinance, and a fixed rate loan. An escrow account is funded at settlement and the servicer draws from it each month for the difference between the payment at the note rate and the payment at the buydown rate. Two points decide most files: the borrower must qualify at the note rate, not the reduced rate, and a buydown funded by an interested party counts against the 6 percent interested party contribution limit.
fha-temporary-buydown.section: HUD Handbook 4000.1, Part W of a wholesale FHA guideline current to 2026-10-15
fha-temporary-buydown.overlayReality: At the lender whose matrix I verified this against, temporary buydowns are available only through the wholesale brokered channel and not through its Select Partner channel. Which channel your originator uses can therefore decide whether the structure is available to you at all, and that is not something most borrowers know to ask.

fha-two-fha-loans.question: Can I have two FHA loans at once?
fha-two-fha-loans.judgmentNeeded: The relocation and family-size exceptions are where this gets interesting. Closed any?

va-appraisal-tidewater.question: What is Tidewater and what happens if the VA appraisal comes in low?
va-appraisal-tidewater.judgmentNeeded: Tidewater gives a chance to supply comps before the value is issued. Most agents have never heard of it.

va-assumability.question: Can someone assume my VA loan?
va-assumability.judgmentNeeded: The sleeper asset. A low-rate assumable loan is a selling advantage. What does the assumption process actually take, and what happens to entitlement?

va-cash-out-refinance.question: How much equity can I take out with a VA cash-out refinance?

va-certificate-of-eligibility.question: What is a Certificate of Eligibility and how do I get one?
va-certificate-of-eligibility.judgmentNeeded: How fast can you actually pull a COE, and what slows it down?

va-condo-approval.question: Does the condo have to be VA approved?

va-dti-compensating.question: What debt-to-income ratio will VA allow?
